static_traits.name: Ma Jie
static_traits.family_status: Father died when the client was 2; the rest Not mentioned
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no psychotherapy or psychiatric treatment received in the past
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, able to self-reflect, fairly cooperative; calm tone, tending toward self-reproach and negative self-labeling

basic_info.main_problem: I love fishing very much, but I keep worrying I will never catch anything again.
basic_info.core_demands: The fear of losing the ability to fish has become overwhelming and has affected my enjoyment of this activity, so I am seeking counseling for help.
growth_experiences: Family-of-origin event: the client's Father died when they were 2, growing up long-term in an environment lacking paternal support; this early loss may have brought persistent Loneliness and a sense of support deprivation.

Academic experience: noticing Declining grades at the start of this school year, then labeling myself 'lazy, ineffective'; when evenings and weekends lacked structure, this self-label and negative emotions intensified, producing a cycle of increased sleep, guilt and Decreased drive; tried improving by setting alarms and making Learning plans, but with limited effect.

core_beliefs: I am not good enough, unable to succeed at anything

special_situations.event: On the most recent fishing trip, encountered multiple challenges, hard to catch fish
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I meet difficulties or have no catch while fishing, it proves I have no ability, and I will never catch fish again in the future
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Improves technique and reduces failures by watching tutorial videos and asking other anglers for advice
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will never catch fish again

special_situations.event: Every time he thinks about going fishing, intense worry and fear surge up
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I feel Anxiety when thinking about fishing, it means I am not suited to continue this activity
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Checking tutorials and seeking advice beforehand to reduce uncertainty, but Anxiety persists
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will fail again; going will bring no fun at all

special_situations.event: Grades slipping since this school year began
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Once grades drop, it shows I am essentially lazy and incapable
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Sets alarms and makes study plans, trying to correct herself with stricter self-demands
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am a lazy waste; I am not good enough, nothing will succeed

special_situations.event: Unstructured evenings and weekends without Learning tasks
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: I should always be efficient; if there is no output I am worthless
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Forcibly makes strict plans for oneself, but soon procrastinates again and sleeps more
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I should not rest, I should work harder, otherwise I am just a failure

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be recognized as capable, and maintain a sense of control and self-esteem in important domains (such as fishing, studies)
core_conflict.fear: Fearing failure and being negated, being seen as 'lazy/incapable', thereby losing the sense of worth and enjoyment
defense_goal: Constrains himself through self-criticism and high standards to avoid failure
Reducing uncertainty and the risk of being negated by increasing preparation and Learning
Avoids revealing worries to family and friends to prevent being judged or shamed

object_relations.self_representation: A child who has lost support, longing to be seen and supported
object_relations.object_representation: The absent Father or an object unable to provide stable support
A harsh critic (internalized external standards and expectations)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor explores the client's negative self-evaluation and failure experiences
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Internalizing the outside world's 'must be efficient and successful' standard into harsh self-judgment, believing that any slight inadequacy equals being a failure
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Use a gentle, Empathy and non-judgmental tone; acknowledge their pain, invite them to specify the experience; help identify the voice of self-attack and distance from it.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When advised to share fears with family and friends and seek feedback
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Worrying that exposing vulnerability will be looked down upon or labeled 'lazy/incapable'
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Gradually expose with a safe and permissive posture; suggest small-step verification, first sharing one small, concrete worry with the most trusted friend.

manifestations: Father died when I was 2; family-of-origin support missing
Not yet sharing my Fear and vulnerability with close fishing friends
outcomes: Difficulty gaining connection and support at important events

manifestations: Worrying I can never enjoy fishing again
Every time thinking of fishing, fear takes over and the joy is stripped away

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Fully attributes grade decline to own lack of effort
Emphasizing 'I am not good enough' in counseling and worrying change is impossible

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'. Language manifestations include: 'I must/should...', 'Everyone is like this', and so on.
manifestations: Believing 'I should always be efficient' during unstructured periods, otherwise being a failure
Using 'I should not rest, I should work harder'-type self-Demands

exception_events.target_problem: On evenings and weekends without Learning tasks, the client usually self-labels as lazy, procrastinates and sleeps too much, then feels guilt and Decreased drive.
exception_events.unique_outcome: The client says there were several times they could complete homework on time, and in those moments the goals were clearer and they had more confidence in themselves.
exception_events.reason: Clue: when goals were more specific and Self-efficacy slightly higher, performance different from usual appeared (more engaged and completing tasks).

positive_force: Able to complete tasks when goals are clear and confidence rises
Willing to seek help and learn (watches tutorials, asks anglers for advice, makes plans)
Positive attitude, willing to try reality testing and cognitive restructuring
negative_force: Catastrophizing and predicting the future leading to avoidance and Anxiety
Low motivation and excessive sleep during unstructured periods
Keeps silent about others' support, lacking external feedback

target_behavior.behavior: Strong worry about fishing failure and catastrophic thinking
antecedent: The most recent fishing trip met multiple challenges and has not yet managed a smooth catch
target_behavior.core_reason: Based on the cognitive biases of overgeneralization and predicting the future, treating one or a few unsuccessful attempts as permanent failure.
target_behavior.function: Avoids potential failure and negative emotions; tries to control outcomes in advance through worry
target_behavior.consequence: Fishing enjoyment significantly decreased, Persistent anxiety, difficulty enjoying the activity

target_behavior.behavior: Self-labeling and self-criticism (e.g. 'I am lazy waste' 'I am not good enough')
antecedent: Grades declining since this school year started
target_behavior.core_reason: Introjected high standards and all-or-nothing thinking, treating short-term performance as global self-worth.
target_behavior.function: Uses self-punishment to drive change or prevent others' criticism
target_behavior.consequence: Worsening Low mood and guilt, further procrastination and loss of motivation

antecedent: Evenings and weekends without Learning tasks or structure
Feeling low and helpless after self-criticism
target_behavior.core_reason: Turning outward action energy against the self through Retroflection, using sleep to escape pressure and failure feelings.
target_behavior.function: Briefly escaping Anxiety and guilt, seeking temporary comfort
target_behavior.consequence: Tasks pile up and motivation drops further, forming a vicious cycle
